questions.q: How do you open the Expression dialog box on a report item property?
options: Right-click the property (or select its fx button) and choose Expression
Press Ctrl+E anywhere on the design surface
Only from the File menu, before any report item is selected
Expressions can only be typed directly into the RDL's XML
questions.explain: Whenever a property accepts an expression, you'll see an fx button, or you can right-click a text box and select Expression — both open the same Expression dialog box.

questions.q: What does the Category tree in the Expression dialog box contain?
options: Built-in collections like Parameters, Fields (Expressions), Datasets, and Variables, plus a Common Functions node
A list of every report in the current project
Only color names for font and fill properties
A history of expressions you've previously typed
questions.explain: Category is the left-hand tree: the built-in collections (Parameters, Fields (Expressions), Datasets, Variables, Operators) and Common Functions, which expands into Text, Date & Time, Math, and more.

questions.q: What happens when you double-click an item in the Item list?
options: It's inserted into the expression text area at the cursor position
It immediately closes the dialog and applies the expression
It deletes that item from the Category tree
Nothing — you must type the function name manually
questions.explain: Double-clicking an item in the Item list inserts it into the expression you're building — you pick functions and fields rather than typing their names from memory.

questions.q: What does the Description/Example panel show when you select a function like Left?
options: What the function does, plus a real working example expression that uses it
The full source code of the function
A list of every report that already uses that function
Nothing — that panel only appears for Fields, not functions
questions.explain: Selecting an item like Left shows its description ("Returns a string containing a specified number of characters...") and a working example, such as =Left(Fields!Description.Value,4).

questions.q: What subcategories does Common Functions expand into?
options: Text, Date & Time, Math, Inspection, Program Flow, Aggregate, Financial, Conversion, and Miscellaneous
Only Text and Math
Fields, Parameters, and Datasets
Report Server, Web Portal, and Subscriptions
questions.explain: Common Functions is a Category subtree covering the built-in function groups you'll use across expressions: string, date/time, math, decision logic, aggregation, and more.
